di-rio-de-pernambuco.name: Diário de Pernambuco
di-rio-de-pernambuco.summary: Newspaper published in Recife, Brazil since 1825, the oldest continuously circulating daily in Latin America and in the Portuguese language.

kasato-maru.name: Kasato Maru
kasato-maru.summary: A Japanese ship that in 1908 carried the first official group of Japanese immigrants to Brazil, arriving at the port of Santos and starting continuous Japanese migration there.

jornal-do-commercio.name: Jornal do Commercio
jornal-do-commercio.summary: A newspaper published in Rio de Janeiro from 1827 until 2016, founded by French journalist Pierre Plancher and once the oldest newspaper in circulation in South America.

oscar-comettant.name: Oscar Comettant
oscar-comettant.summary: A 19th-century French composer, musicologist and traveller (1819 to 1898).

pot-au-feu.name: Pot-au-feu
pot-au-feu.summary: A French dish of slowly boiled meat and vegetables, usually served as broth first and then the meat and vegetables, familiar throughout France with many regional variations.

puchero.name: Puchero
puchero.summary: A stew originally from Spain, similar to cocido, made in Spain and across Latin America and the Philippines with local ingredients; its name comes from the Spanish word for the pot it was cooked in.

escola-nacional-de-belas-artes.name: Escola Nacional de Belas Artes
escola-nacional-de-belas-artes.summary: Founded by royal decree in 1816 as the Royal School of Sciences, Arts and Crafts, this institution later became Brazil's Imperial Academy and then the National School of Fine Arts.

john-vi-of-portugal.name: John VI of Portugal
john-vi-of-portugal.summary: John VI of Portugal: King of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves (1767–1826) who fled to Brazil when Napoleon's forces invaded Portugal and later became titular Emperor of Brazil.

imperial-academy-of-fine-arts-brazil.name: Imperial Academy of Fine Arts
imperial-academy-of-fine-arts-brazil.summary: An institution of higher learning in the arts in Rio de Janeiro, founded by King João VI, which became the leading centre of art education in Brazil under Emperor Dom Pedro II.

pedro-ii-of-brazil.name: Pedro II of Brazil
pedro-ii-of-brazil.summary: Second and final emperor of Brazil, known as 'the Magnanimous,' who reigned from 1831 to 1889, presiding over the longest and most stable reign in Brazilian history.

amazon-theatre.name: Teatro Amazonas
amazon-theatre.summary: An opera house in Manaus, Brazil, built during the Amazon rubber boom, home to an annual opera festival and philharmonic orchestra, later named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2026.

pedro-am-rico.name: Pedro Américo
pedro-am-rico.summary: Brazilian painter, novelist, scientist and politician (1843–1905), regarded as one of Brazil's most important academic painters, known for civic and heroic works like Battle of Avaí.

victor-meirelles.name: Victor Meirelles
victor-meirelles.summary: Brazilian history painter (1832–1903) trained in Europe, who became a favorite artist of Emperor Pedro II and helped create visual symbols of Brazil's history.

grandjean-de-montigny.name: Grandjean de Montigny
grandjean-de-montigny.summary: A French architect, 1776 to 1850, who shaped the development of architecture in Brazil after moving there, and a patron of the Brazilian Academy of Fine Arts.

museu-nacional-de-belas-artes.name: Museu Nacional de Belas Artes
museu-nacional-de-belas-artes.summary: National art museum in Rio de Janeiro established in 1937, its collection rooted in the Portuguese Royal Collection brought to Brazil in 1808, now Brazil's leading museum of Brazilian art.

joachim-lebreton.name: Joachim Lebreton
joachim-lebreton.summary: French professor, public administrator and legislator who lived from 1760 to 1819.

ionic-order.name: Ionic order
ionic-order.summary: One of the three classical architectural orders, alongside the Doric and Corinthian, identified by columns with volute-scrolled capitals and narrower columns than the Doric.

rio-de-janeiro-botanical-garden.name: Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden
rio-de-janeiro-botanical-garden.summary: A botanical garden founded in 1808 by King John VI of Portugal, originally meant for acclimatizing spices, now home to thousands of plant species and an avenue of royal palms.

battle-of-acosta-u.name: Battle of Acosta Ñu
battle-of-acosta-u.summary: An 1869 battle, the last major engagement of the Paraguayan War, in which about 3,500 poorly armed Paraguayans, mostly boys, old men and wounded, faced 20,000 Brazilian and Argentine soldiers; remembered in Paraguay as the Children's Battle.

paraguayan-war.name: Paraguayan War
paraguayan-war.summary: The deadliest interstate war in Latin American history, fought 1864 to 1870 between Paraguay and the allied forces of Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay, ending in Paraguay's defeat and huge civilian losses.

cisplatine-war.name: Cisplatine War
cisplatine-war.summary: A 1820s war between the Empire of Brazil and the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata over the Banda Oriental, ending in the independence of Uruguay.

united-provinces-of-the-r-o-de-la-plata.name: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
united-provinces-of-the-r-o-de-la-plata.summary: The state that succeeded the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata after the 1810 May Revolution, spanning Argentina's independence and civil wars before becoming today's Argentine Republic.
united-provinces-of-the-r-o-de-la-plata.source_title: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata

banda-oriental.name: Banda Oriental
banda-oriental.summary: The historical name for territories east of the Uruguay River and north of the Río de la Plata, now Uruguay and parts of Brazil, disputed between the Spanish and Portuguese empires.

cisplatina.name: Cisplatina
cisplatina.summary: A Brazilian province from 1821 to 1828, created by the Luso-Brazilian invasion of the Banda Oriental, which became independent as Uruguay in 1828.

pedro-i-of-brazil.name: Pedro I of Brazil
pedro-i-of-brazil.summary: Founder and first ruler of the Empire of Brazil (1822–1831) and briefly King of Portugal in 1826, known as 'the Liberator'; declared Brazil's independence in 1822.

bahia.name: Bahia
bahia.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil holding about 7% of the country's population, with its capital Salvador on the Bay of All Saints.

maranh-o.name: Maranhão
maranh-o.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil with about 7 million people, bordering the Atlantic Ocean, home to the dunes of Lençóis and the UNESCO World Heritage city of São Luís.

par.name: Pará
par.summary: A large state in northern Brazil crossed by the lower Amazon River, with its capital at Belém near the river's estuary.

piau.name: Piauí
piau.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil with the shortest coastline of any coastal Brazilian state, colonized inland before the coast, and home to the rock-art-rich Serra da Capivara National Park.

brazilian-naval-revolts.name: Brazilian Naval Revolts
brazilian-naval-revolts.summary: Armed mutinies by Brazilian navy admirals against President Floriano Peixoto's claimed unconstitutional hold on power, driven by elite rivalries and lingering monarchist sentiment.

war-of-canudos.name: War of Canudos
war-of-canudos.summary: An 1896–1897 conflict between the First Brazilian Republic and residents of the settlement of Canudos, led by the millenarian preacher Antônio Conselheiro, seen as a monarchist threat to the young republic.

contestado-war.name: Contestado War
contestado-war.summary: A Brazilian guerrilla war between settlers and state-backed landowners, lasting from 1912 to 1916, fueled by land disputes and religious fervor among rebellious caboclos.

lu-s-alves-de-lima-e-silva-duke-of-caxia.name: Duke of Caxias
lu-s-alves-de-lima-e-silva-duke-of-caxia.summary: Title of Luís Alves de Lima e Silva (1803-1880), a Brazilian army officer and monarchist who commanded loyalist and allied forces through several 19th-century wars.
lu-s-alves-de-lima-e-silva-duke-of-caxia.source_title: Luís Alves de Lima e Silva, Duke of Caxias

francisco-solano-l-pez.name: Francisco Solano López
francisco-solano-l-pez.summary: Paraguayan statesman and military officer (1826/27–1870), president of Paraguay from 1862 to 1870, killed in action during the Paraguayan War, the only Paraguayan president to die in combat.

gaston-count-of-eu.name: Gaston, Count of Eu
gaston-count-of-eu.summary: French Orléans prince (1842–1922) who commanded Allied forces in the final phase of the Paraguayan War and became a key figure in Brazilian imperial affairs through his marriage to Princess Isabel.

bernardino-caballero.name: Bernardino Caballero
bernardino-caballero.summary: A Paraguayan general who fought in the Paraguayan War and served as president from 1880 to 1886 after a coup, later founding the Colorado Party in 1887.

thirty-three-orientals.name: Thirty-Three Orientals
thirty-three-orientals.summary: A revolutionary group led by Juan Antonio Lavalleja and Manuel Oribe whose 1825 uprising against Brazilian rule began the Cisplatine War and led to the founding of modern Uruguay.

juan-antonio-lavalleja.name: Juan Antonio Lavalleja
juan-antonio-lavalleja.summary: Uruguayan revolutionary, military general and political figure (1784–1853), born in Minas, a region later named after him.

battle-of-rinc-n.name: Battle of Rincón
battle-of-rinc-n.summary: A battle fought on 24 September 1825 near modern Uruguay's Río Negro Department, the first clash between Fructuoso Rivera's rebel forces and troops loyal to the Empire of Brazil in the Cisplatine War.

battle-of-sarand.name: Battle of Sarandí
battle-of-sarand.summary: A battle fought on 12 October 1825 near the Arroyo Sarandí in Uruguay, a decisive victory for the Oriental rebels over the Empire of Brazil.

deodoro-da-fonseca.name: Deodoro da Fonseca
deodoro-da-fonseca.summary: A Brazilian military officer and politician (1827-1892) who led the 1889 coup that deposed Emperor Pedro II, becoming Brazil's first president before resigning in 1891.

first-brazilian-republic.name: First Brazilian Republic
first-brazilian-republic.summary: Brazilian state from 1889 to 1930, begun by a coup that deposed Emperor Pedro II and ended by the 1930 revolution that brought Getúlio Vargas to power.

republic-of-the-sword.name: Republic of the Sword
republic-of-the-sword.summary: The early, military-dominated period of the First Brazilian Republic (1889-1894) under Marshals Deodoro da Fonseca and Floriano Peixoto, marked by dictatorship and an economic crisis.

floriano-peixoto.name: Floriano Peixoto
floriano-peixoto.summary: Brazilian military officer and politician (1839–1895), nicknamed the Iron Marshal, who served as Brazil's first vice president and then its second president, from 1891 to 1894.

volunt-rios-da-p-tria.name: Fatherland Volunteer Corps
volunt-rios-da-p-tria.summary: Volunteer military units created by decree of the Empire of Brazil in 1865 to fight in the Paraguayan War and strengthen the Imperial Brazilian Army.

alfredo-d-escragnolle-taunay-viscount-of.name: Viscount of Taunay
alfredo-d-escragnolle-taunay-viscount-of.summary: Brazilian writer, military engineer and politician, 1843 to 1899, known for the novel "Inocência" and an account of an episode in the Paraguayan War described as a masterpiece of that war's literature.
alfredo-d-escragnolle-taunay-viscount-of.source_title: Alfredo d'Escragnolle Taunay, Viscount of Taunay

jos-gervasio-artigas.name: José Gervasio Artigas
jos-gervasio-artigas.summary: Uruguayan soldier and statesman (1764–1850) regarded as Uruguay's founding hero, who fought Spanish rule and later formed a federal alliance of provinces before dying in exile in Paraguay.

machado-de-assis.name: Machado de Assis
machado-de-assis.summary: Pioneering Brazilian novelist, poet and playwright, 1839 to 1908, widely regarded as Brazil's greatest writer, who founded the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1897.

maria-firmina-dos-reis.name: Maria Firmina dos Reis
maria-firmina-dos-reis.summary: Brazilian author (1822–1917) considered the country's first black female novelist; her 1859 novel Úrsula, told through the lens of slavery, is regarded as Brazil's first abolitionist novel.

cruz-e-sousa.name: Cruz e Sousa
cruz-e-sousa.summary: Brazilian poet and journalist (1861–1898), descended from African slaves, known as one of Brazil's first Symbolist poets and nicknamed the 'Black Dante'.

mart-n-fierro.name: Martín Fierro
mart-n-fierro.summary: A 2,316-line epic poem by Argentine writer José Hernández, published in 1872 and 1879, celebrating the gaucho and widely seen as a touchstone of Argentine national identity.

jos-hern-ndez-writer.name: José Hernández
jos-hern-ndez-writer.summary: Argentine journalist, poet, and politician (1834–1886) best known for the epic poem Martín Fierro; his birthday is now Argentina's national Tradition Day.

alberto-blest-gana.name: Alberto Blest Gana
alberto-blest-gana.summary: Chilean novelist and diplomat (1830–1920), considered the father of the Chilean novel.

gon-alves-de-magalh-es-viscount-of-aragu.name: Gonçalves de Magalhães
gon-alves-de-magalh-es-viscount-of-aragu.summary: Brazilian poet, playwright, doctor and diplomat (1811–1882) considered the founder of Romanticism in Brazilian literature and a pioneer of its theatre.
gon-alves-de-magalh-es-viscount-of-aragu.source_title: Gonçalves de Magalhães, Viscount of Araguaia

s-o-lu-s-maranh-o.name: São Luís
s-o-lu-s-maranh-o.summary: Capital of the Brazilian state of Maranhão, founded by France as Saint-Louis-de-Maragnan and the only Brazilian state capital founded by that country; its 17th-century historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

adolfo-caminha.name: Adolfo Caminha
adolfo-caminha.summary: Brazilian Naturalist novelist (1867–1897) famous for the controversial novel Bom-Crioulo, which deals with race and homosexuality.

bom-crioulo.name: Bom-Crioulo
bom-crioulo.summary: An 1895 novel by Brazilian writer Adolfo Caminha about an ex-slave sailor's love for a young cabin boy, considered the first major literary work on homosexuality published in Brazil.

jules-verne.name: Jules Verne
jules-verne.summary: French novelist, poet and playwright, 1828 to 1905, whose adventure novels such as Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas made him one of the most translated authors ever.

lvares-de-azevedo.name: Álvares de Azevedo
lvares-de-azevedo.summary: Brazilian Romantic poet, story writer and essayist (1831-1852), a leading figure of Ultra-Romanticism and Gothic literature in Brazil whose works were published only after his early death.

noite-na-taverna.name: Noite na Taverna
noite-na-taverna.summary: An 1855 short story collection by Brazilian author Álvares de Azevedo, published posthumously under the pen name Job Stern and considered one of Brazilian literature's most influential Gothic works.

lira-dos-vinte-anos.name: Lira dos Vinte Anos
lira-dos-vinte-anos.summary: A poetry anthology by Brazilian Romantic writer Álvares de Azevedo, published in 1853 after his death, divided into contrasting sentimental and morbid, ironic sections.

lord-byron.name: Lord Byron
lord-byron.summary: A British Romantic poet (1788–1824) known for works like Don Juan and Childe Harold's Pilgrimage, who died in 1824 from a fever while leading a campaign in the Greek War of Independence.

alfred-de-musset.name: Alfred de Musset
alfred-de-musset.summary: French dramatist, poet and novelist, 1810 to 1857, known for his autobiographical novel "The Confession of a Child of the Century".

os-sert-es.name: Os Sertões
os-sert-es.summary: A 1902 book by Brazilian author Euclides da Cunha mixing science and literature to recount the 1893 to 1897 war against the messianic-led settlement of Canudos in Bahia's backlands.

castro-alves.name: Castro Alves
castro-alves.summary: A Brazilian poet and playwright (1847–1871) famed for abolitionist and republican poems, seen as a leading voice against slavery in the Romantic era.

joaquim-nabuco.name: Joaquim Nabuco
joaquim-nabuco.summary: Brazilian statesman, diplomat and leading abolitionist (1849–1910) who came from a slaveholding family yet fought to end slavery.

alu-sio-azevedo.name: Aluísio Azevedo
alu-sio-azevedo.summary: Brazilian novelist, caricaturist, diplomat and playwright (1857-1913) who introduced Naturalism to Brazil with the 1881 novel O Mulato and founded the Brazilian Academy of Letters.

jos-ver-ssimo.name: José Veríssimo
jos-ver-ssimo.summary: Brazilian writer, educator, journalist and literary critic (1857–1916), and a founding member of the Brazilian Academy of Letters.

raul-pompeia.name: Raul Pompeia
raul-pompeia.summary: Brazilian novelist and short story writer (1863 to 1895), best known for the Impressionist novel O Ateneu; he died by suicide on Christmas Day 1895.

em-lia-freitas.name: Emília Freitas
em-lia-freitas.summary: Brazilian novelist, poet, and teacher (1855–1908) who wrote what is considered the first Brazilian fantasy novel, A Rainha do Ignoto (1899), about a utopian society of women.

horacio-de-almeida.name: Horácio de Almeida
horacio-de-almeida.summary: Deputy Provedor of Human Rights in Timor-Leste since January 2015, born 16 April 1975 in Uato-Lari, Viqueque.

o-tico-tico.name: O Tico-Tico
o-tico-tico.summary: A weekly Brazilian children's magazine published from 1905 to 1977, the first in Brazil to print comics, whose readers included several noted Brazilian writers.

national-library-of-brazil.name: Biblioteca Nacional
national-library-of-brazil.summary: Brazil's national library in Rio de Janeiro, considered by UNESCO the largest library in Latin America, holding about 9 million items and pioneering library science courses in the region.

national-museum-of-brazil.name: National Museum of Brazil
national-museum-of-brazil.summary: Brazil's oldest scientific institution, housed in a former royal and imperial palace in Rio de Janeiro; founded in 1818 as the Royal Museum, it was largely destroyed by fire in 2018.

hermann-von-ihering.name: Hermann von Ihering
hermann-von-ihering.summary: German-Brazilian doctor and ornithologist (1850–1930) who helped found São Paulo's Museu Paulista and became its first director.

mil-goeldi.name: Émil Goeldi
mil-goeldi.summary: Swiss-Brazilian naturalist and zoologist (1859–1917), father of the noted Brazilian engraver Oswaldo Goeldi.

jo-o-baptista-de-lacerda.name: João Baptista de Lacerda
jo-o-baptista-de-lacerda.summary: Brazilian physician (1846–1915) and one of the country's pioneering biomedical scientists in experimental physiology and pharmacology.

louis-couty.name: Louis Couty
louis-couty.summary: A French doctor and physiologist (1854–1884) who worked at Rio de Janeiro's National Museum, studied curare and other toxins, and wrote an early sociological study, Slavery in Brazil.

napoleon.name: Napoleon
napoleon.summary: French emperor from 1804 to 1814, and briefly in 1815, who rose to power as a general during the French Revolution and led sweeping military campaigns across Europe and the Middle East.

isabel-princess-imperial-of-brazil.name: Princess Isabel of Brazil
isabel-princess-imperial-of-brazil.summary: Princess Imperial and heir to the Brazilian throne (1846–1921) who served as regent three times and signed the 1888 law abolishing slavery; she went into exile after the 1889 coup that ended the monarchy.

lei-urea.name: Golden Law
lei-urea.summary: Brazil's 1888 law abolishing slavery, signed by Princess Isabel while acting as regent; Brazil was the last country in the Americas to end slavery.

l-bero-badar.name: Líbero Badaró
l-bero-badar.summary: Italian-born Brazilian doctor, botanist, journalist and politician (c. 1798–1830).

miguel-i-of-portugal.name: Miguel I of Portugal
miguel-i-of-portugal.summary: King of Portugal from 1828 to 1834 who seized the throne from his niece Maria II, sparking the Portuguese Liberal Wars before his eventual exile.

maria-ii-of-portugal.name: Maria II of Portugal
maria-ii-of-portugal.summary: Queen of Portugal from 1826 to 1828 and again from 1834 to 1853, nicknamed 'the Educator'; she became queen at age seven after her father abdicated in her favour.

teixeira-mendes.name: Teixeira Mendes
teixeira-mendes.summary: Brazilian philosopher and mathematician (1855–1927) credited with creating Brazil's national motto, "Order and Progress," and the flag it appears on.

auguste-comte.name: Auguste Comte
auguste-comte.summary: French philosopher (1798–1857) who coined the term sociology and founded the doctrine of positivism, influencing thinkers such as John Stuart Mill.

religion-of-humanity.name: Religion of Humanity
religion-of-humanity.summary: A secular religion proposed by French philosopher Auguste Comte (1798–1857), whose followers built "chapels of Humanity" in Brazil and France.

mal-revolt.name: Malê revolt
mal-revolt.summary: 1835 uprising of enslaved and freed African Muslims in Salvador, Brazil, timed to a religious festival, and the largest slave rebellion in Brazilian history.

proclamation-of-the-republic-brazil.name: Proclamation of the Republic
proclamation-of-the-republic-brazil.summary: The 1889 military coup that ended Brazil's constitutional monarchy and Emperor Pedro II's reign, establishing the First Brazilian Republic.

neo-scholasticism.name: Neo-scholasticism
neo-scholasticism.summary: A revival and development of medieval Scholasticism in Catholic theology, also called neo-scholastic Thomism for its debt to Thomas Aquinas, beginning in the late 19th century.

aeterni-patris.name: Aeterni Patris
aeterni-patris.summary: An 1879 encyclical by Pope Leo XIII aimed at reviving Scholastic philosophy, especially the teachings of Thomas Aquinas, in Catholic schools.

leuven.name: Leuven
leuven.summary: A city in Flemish Brabant, Belgium, and a university city since 1425, the oldest in the Low Countries, now home to KU Leuven and the headquarters of brewer Anheuser-Busch InBev.

benjamin-constant-military.name: Benjamin Constant
benjamin-constant-military.summary: Brazilian military officer and positivist political thinker (1836–1891) who founded Brazil's positivist movement and helped organize the coup that established the republic.

c-ndido-rondon.name: Cândido Rondon
c-ndido-rondon.summary: Brazilian military officer (1865–1958) known for exploring Mato Grosso and the western Amazon and for lifelong support of Indigenous Brazilians; first director of Brazil's Indian Protection Service, with the state of Rondônia named after him.

batuque-brazil.name: Batuque
batuque-brazil.summary: 19th-century Afro-Brazilian drumming ceremonies that drew large crowds of enslaved Africans despite police repression, later giving rise to samba and influencing capoeira.

capoeira.name: Capoeira
capoeira.summary: An Afro-Brazilian martial art blending dance, acrobatics, music and spirituality, rooted in the Angolan Bantu tradition and once criminalized before Brazil legalized it in 1937.

maracatu.name: Maracatu
maracatu.summary: A group of Afro-Brazilian performance genres from Pernambuco in northeastern Brazil, including the nation-style and rural-style forms.

rio-grande-do-sul.name: Rio Grande do Sul
rio-grande-do-sul.summary: A southern Brazilian state bordering Uruguay and Argentina, with capital Porto Alegre, shaped by Guarani and Kaingang peoples, Jesuit and Azorean settlers, and German and Italian migration.

hermann-blumenau.name: Hermann Blumenau
hermann-blumenau.summary: A German pharmacist who founded the city of Blumenau in Brazil's Santa Catarina state; he lived from 1819 to 1899.

blumenau.name: Blumenau
blumenau.summary: A city in southern Brazil founded by the German chemist Hermann Blumenau in the mid-19th century, known for its German heritage and Oktoberfest celebration.

mackenzie-presbyterian-university.name: Mackenzie Presbyterian University
mackenzie-presbyterian-university.summary: Private Brazilian university founded in 1870 by Pennsylvania missionaries as the American School, now a leading private institution whose graduates include governors and executives.

joinville.name: Joinville
joinville.summary: Now the largest city in Santa Catarina, southern Brazil, with a population of about 598,000 and one of the highest standards of living in Latin America.

princess-francisca-of-brazil.name: Princess Francisca of Brazil
princess-francisca-of-brazil.summary: A princess of the Empire of Brazil, daughter of Emperor Dom Pedro I, who became Princess of Joinville after marrying François d'Orléans, son of French king Louis Philippe I.

fran-ois-d-orl-ans-prince-of-joinville.name: François d'Orléans, Prince of Joinville
fran-ois-d-orl-ans-prince-of-joinville.summary: Third son of King Louis Philippe of France and admiral of the French Navy (1818–1900), known for bringing Napoleon's remains back from Saint Helena and for his watercolor art.

brazil_southern_cone-industrial-art-001: Royal School of Sciences, Arts and Crafts
brazil_southern_cone-industrial-art-005: Royal School of Sciences, Arts and Crafts
brazil_southern_cone-industrial-art-007: Botanical Garden of Rio de Janeiro
brazil_southern_cone-industrial-war-006: United Provinces of the Río de la Plata
brazil_southern_cone-industrial-war-002: Prince Gaston of Orleans, the Count of Eu
brazil_southern_cone-industrial-science-: National Museum in Rio de Janeiro
